newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's CCU says plans to invest $100 mln.
newsitem.headline: Chile's CCU says plans to invest $100 mln.

text.p: Compania Cervecerias Unidas (CCU), Chile's biggest beer producer, will invest over $100 million in 1997, the firm's top official said Tuesday.
"We have been investing a bit over $100 million on average over the past five years, and this will be the same in 1997," CCU general manager Francisco Perez Mackenna told Reuters in an interview.
A $30-million chunk of CCU's investment spending will go to expanding its wine maker, Vina San Pedro

"The most important news is the change of plans for San Pedro, where we are going to boost our acreage planted with vines and we are also going to increase our wine-making capacity," Perez Mackenna said.
He said CCU hoped San Pedro's exports will rise to more than 1.5 million cases this year from 1.2 million cases in 1996. San Pedro is already Chile's third-largest wine exporter.

CCU's beer brands have about 90 percent of the Chilean market. Via Embotelladoras Chilenas Unidas (Ecusa), a joint venture with Argentine firm Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (Baesa), it also bottles and distributes a range of mineral waters and soft drinks.
CCU operates two beer plants in Argentina, in the provinces of Santa Fe and Salta, whose produce Baesa distributes in Buenos Aires and CCU throughout the rest of the country.
CCU's other foreign venture is a share in the Karlovacka Pivovara brewery in Croatia.

The firm's main intention outside Chile is currently to consolidate its position in the Argentine market, where it has a 12-percent share, although it is also studying possible new investments in Croatia and other parts of Eastern Europe, Perez Mackenna said.
CCU plans new expansions at its Santa Fe plant this year, and has bought the land to build a brewery in Buenos Aires which it hopes will begin to produce by 2000.

"We think the beer business is going to expand faster in Argentina than in Chile for two reasons," Perez Mackenna said, "First because the Argentine market is growing more quickly. Second because there we have room to increase our market share."
He added, "In five years we hope to have between 18 percent and 20 percent of the Argentine market."
CCU expects 15 percent of its income to come from its Argentine operations in 1997, up from 10 percent last year.
The company expects its profits to keep rising this year, after a good first quarter return of $30 million, up 36 from the same period in 1996.

"We are going to have a good first half and that is going to give us a good current account. Also, the economy is going to have to grow more strongly in the second half than in the first," Perez Mackenna said. ((--Santiago Newsroom +562 6995595 x213))
